The decision to keep or shorten the tea-serving ceremony depends on several factors, including cultural traditions, the size of the family, the overall wedding schedule, and the couple’s vision for the event. Here are some considerations to help you decide: ### **Reasons to Keep It (or Modify It Slightly):** 1. **Cultural Significance** – If this is a cherished tradition in your family (e.g., a gesture of respect, blessing, or unity), preserving it can add emotional depth to the wedding. 2. **Symbolism** – Serving tea one by one can symbolize care, gratitude, and connection, which may be meaningful for the couple and guests. 3. **Family Bonding** – If the elders are close-knit and enjoy the ritual, it could be a heartwarming moment rather than a time drain. ### **Reasons to Shorten It:** 1. **Time Constraints** – If the wedding schedule is tight (e.g., long speeches, a late start, or a busy reception), an hour may feel excessive, especially if guests are eager to eat or socialize. 2. **Guest Comfort** – Some elders (or guests) may feel fatigued waiting in line for so long, especially if they’ve already traveled or attended other events. 3. **Modern Adjustments** – If the couple wants a more streamlined ceremony, they could: - **Group elders** (e.g., by family branches) to reduce the line. - **Shorten the ritual** (e.g., just a quick blessing or handshake instead of a full tea ceremony). - **Schedule it earlier** (e.g., before the main ceremony) to avoid delays. ### **Alternative Ideas:** - **Hybrid Approach:** Keep the tradition but make it more efficient (e.g., a shorter, more symbolic tea exchange). - **Delegate:** Assign a family member or trusted person to oversee the process to keep it moving smoothly. - **Combine with Another Ritual:** Merge it with a family photo session or a short blessing to save time. ### **Final Thought:** If the ceremony holds deep meaning for the family, it might be worth preserving—just with some adjustments to fit the modern wedding timeline. AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

prediction.raw: I’d give this scenario a **0/1**—meaning it was **not a great decision**, and here’s why: ### **Why It Was Wrong:** 1. **Lack of Communication** – You didn’t discuss the profile with your stepbrother beforehand, even though you knew he enjoyed playing on it. Deleting it without warning was thoughtless, especially since you’d already made an effort to accommodate him. 2. **Emotional Impact** – Even if he wasn’t "full-on crying," the fact that he was upset shows that the profile meant something to him. You didn’t consider how he might feel when you removed it. 3. **Dad’s Perspective** – Your father saw it as disrespectful because you knew he enjoyed the Switch and didn’t ask permission. That’s a reasonable take—sharing your space (even temporarily) usually means some compromise. 4. **No Real Need** – You said you were annoyed by having to switch profiles, but that’s a minor inconvenience compared to the emotional fallout. There were better solutions (e.g., just keeping his profile or asking him to use it less). ### **What You Could Do Now:** - **Apologize sincerely** (not just to your stepbrother, but to your dad too). - **Offer to help him recover his save** (if possible) or at least explain why you did it. - **Avoid repeating the mistake**—next time, discuss boundaries or ask if he’d like to use your Switch. ### **Final Thought:** You didn’t *intend* to hurt him, but the lack of consideration made it a poor choice. A little empathy would’ve gone a long way!
